settings.title: Settings
settings.gpu.title: GPU video compositing
settings.gpu.desc: Uses the graphics card to compose the app screen. Off (default), composition is done by the CPU, which is usually more stable. Turn it on if you prefer GPU acceleration.
settings.restart.notice: Restart the app for the change to take effect.
hotkey.title: Hotkey
hotkey.note.html: Pick a key that DayZ does not use: while the switch is on, the game does not receive that key (C, for example, would stop making you crouch). Prefer F5 to F12 or a combination with Ctrl or Alt.
hotkey.warn: Heads up: the {key} key may have a function inside DayZ. While this tool is on, the game will not recognize that key. If you don't use {key} in the game, you can ignore this warning. If you do, pick a key from F5 to F12 or a combination with Ctrl or Alt plus the key.
howto.title: How to use
autorun.desc.html: Runs on its own by holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>W</kbd> while DayZ is in focus.
autorun.hotkeyHint: Press it in the game to start or stop running.
autorun.step1.html: Keep DayZ open. It shows up under Game window, in the bottom-left corner.
autorun.step2: Turn on Auto Run with the switch above.
autorun.step3: In the game, press the hotkey to run and press it again to stop.
autorun.ready: In the game, press {key} to run.
autorun.active: Holding Shift + W. Press {key} to stop.
clicker.desc: Holds the right mouse button and clicks the left one about 5 times a second, only while DayZ is in focus.
clicker.hotkeyHint: Press it in the game to start or stop the clicks.
clicker.step1: Turn on Auto Clicker with the switch above.
clicker.step2: In the game, press the hotkey to start.
clicker.step3: Press it again to stop. If you leave the game, it pauses by itself.
clicker.ready: In the game, press {key} to start clicking.
clicker.active: Holding the right button and clicking the left. Press {key} to stop.
tool.off.hint: Turn on the switch next to this to use the hotkey.
tool.paused.hint: Go back to DayZ to continue.
server.desc: Did the server go down or restart? You don't need to keep refreshing the DayZ Launcher. Enter the server once and choose: get alerted when it comes back from a restart, or follow its live status (in-game time, queue, players and ping) every minute.
server.offline.hint: Waiting for the server to come back · attempt {attempt}
server.confirming.hint: Making sure it is really online ({done}/{needed})
server.waiting.hint: The server is online right now. You'll be alerted when it restarts and comes back.
server.locked.hint: The server is locked. You'll be alerted when it opens.
server.starting.hint: The server already answers but is still loading. Waiting until it is ready.
server.idle.hint: Server down or restarting? The app checks every second and alerts you with a sound and an on-screen notice as soon as it is really online.
server.title: Server
server.locked.note: The fields are locked because something is on. To change the IP or the ports, first turn off {what}.
server.locked.dep: The on-screen clock uses Live status: while it is off, it stays idle.
server.qport.hint: Leave empty to detect it automatically. Only fill it in if the server is not found.
server.restart.label: Restart alert
server.beta.hint: Feature in testing: we are still tuning how the app decides the server is really back.
live.label: Live status
live.title: Server status
live.off.hint: Turn on to see in-game time, queue, players and ping, updated automatically.
live.version.client: Your game is out of date ({version}). Update DayZ.
live.version.server: Server is out of date: your game ({version}) is newer.
overlay.desc: Shows the in-game time, exactly as the server reports it, in a corner of the screen, on top of DayZ, like an FPS counter.
overlay.label: Game clock
overlay.toggle: Show the game clock on screen
overlay.off.hint: Turn on to always see the in-game time on screen while you play.
overlay.on.hint: Shows on top of DayZ while the game is in focus. While this app is open, it shows a preview.
overlay.noserver.hint: Enter the address in Server Monitor. The clock uses Live status.
overlay.waiting.hint: The clock appears as soon as the server answers.
overlay.pos.title: Position
overlay.pos.hint: Pick the screen corner and, if needed, fine-tune it in pixels.
overlay.fine.hint: Distance from the chosen corner's edge: larger values move the clock away from the edge; negative values push it past the edge.
overlay.note.title: Before you use it
overlay.note.mode.html: In DayZ, use the Windowed or Borderless video mode. In exclusive fullscreen Windows won't let anything show on top of the game.
overlay.note.focus: The clock only shows while DayZ is in focus, so it doesn't sit on top of other programs.
overlay.note.server: The time is whatever the server reports, checked every few seconds while the clock is on.
map.credit: Interactive map provided by {name}; all credit and rights belong to its creators. This app is not affiliated with {name}.
radio.desc.html: On Nasdara (the Badlands map) a radio on 80.0 MHz broadcasts bunker locations and door codes in morse. The app listens to the game's sound and writes it all down for you.
radio.label: Bunker radio
radio.beta.hint: Feature in testing: the decoder was tested with simulated sounds, not yet with the game's real broadcast.
radio.beta.note: Feature in testing, not yet validated against the game's real radio broadcast. If a code comes out wrong, wait for the message to repeat: a digit is only treated as certain once it is heard twice alike.
radio.stopped.hint: Click Listen to the game and keep the radio on 80.0 MHz.
radio.listening.hint: Listening to DayZ's sound only. Keep the in-game radio on 80.0 MHz: it only broadcasts at night.
radio.listening.hint.system: Could not isolate DayZ's sound: listening to all of the PC's sound. Keep other sounds off.
radio.waiting.hint: Open the game: the app listens to its sound only and starts by itself when DayZ shows up.
radio.err.title: Could not listen
radio.err.nosound: Windows did not hand over the PC's sound. Check the audio output and try again.
radio.err.capture: Could not capture the PC's sound ({error}).
radio.how.title: How to use
radio.how.1.html: Turn on a Personal Radio or Base Radio in DayZ and tune it to 80.0 MHz. It only broadcasts at night in the game (sunset to dawn): 3 bunkers per night, and the message repeats every few minutes.
radio.how.2.html: Click Listen to the game. The app listens to the PC's sound and turns the beeps into a map grid and a code.
radio.how.3.html: Go to the bunker, type the code on the keypad by the door and press the key button while the radio is on air.
radio.tips.title: Tips for better listening
radio.tip.1.html: In DayZ, open Options > Sound, turn the effects volume right down and switch the music off: the radio beeps stay loud and everything else goes quiet.
radio.tip.2: The app listens to DayZ's sound only, so music and videos on the PC don't get in the way. If Windows won't let it isolate the game, it says so and listens to all of the PC's sound: then keep other sounds off.
radio.tip.3: Grey code: heard only once, wait for the repeat. It turns solid when every digit is heard twice alike.
radio.results.title: Bunkers heard
radio.results.empty: None yet. Each bunker shows up here as soon as its grid is heard.
radio.results.hint: The grid is the in-game map's: 3 digits east and 3 from the north edge, in 100 m squares.
radio.live.title: Live decoding
radio.live.hint: Each box is a digit: the decoded digit on top, the beeps heard (dot and dash) below. “–” is a digit that did not resolve.
radio.onmap.hint: Opens iZurvive at this bunker’s exact position
radio.badge.once: Heard once, wait for the repeat
radio.badge.part: Heard in part, wait for the repeat
sound.title: Sound alert
sound.hint: Plays when the server is back from a restart.
window.title: Choose the DayZ window
window.sub: Can't find the game? Open DayZ and click refresh.
update.title: New version v{version}
update.howto: The app downloads the update, closes, installs it on its own and opens again already updated, with no installer for you to run. It takes a few minutes, depending on your connection: as soon as the download finishes it restarts, so save what you’re doing.
update.downloading: Downloading the update. You can close this window: the download keeps going and the app only restarts when it finishes.
update.installing: Download complete. The app will close, install the update and open again on its own.
update.error.offline: Couldn’t reach GitHub: no internet or the connection dropped. Check your network and try again.
update.error.server: GitHub isn’t responding right now (or couldn’t find the update file). Try again in a few minutes.
update.error.disk: There isn’t enough free disk space to download the update. Free some space and try again.
update.error.corrupt: The downloaded file was damaged and was discarded. Try downloading again.
update.error.unknown: Couldn’t download or install the update. Try again or download it manually.
update.error.note: The app you’re using keeps working normally.
whatsnew.title: What's new in v{version}
whatsnew.open: See what's new in this version
notice.title: Before you use it
notice.p1: DZ Toolkit sends key presses and mouse clicks to DayZ as if they were yours: Shift + W held down (Auto Run) and the right button held down with repeated left clicks (Auto Clicker).
notice.p2.html: Many servers ban macros and any kind of game automation, and the punishment applies even if BattlEye does not block it. Check your server's rules before turning on any tool.
notice.p3: Use at your own risk. The app does not change or read the game's memory.
toast.keyInUse: The {key} key is being used by another program
toast.keyTaken: {key} is already the key for {feature}. Pick another one.
toast.keyRisky: {key} may have a function in DayZ: while this tool is on, the game will not recognize that key. If you don't use it in the game, you're fine
